answer: To resist sybil attacks, every agent that wants to vote or earn must first deposit a time-locked bond into a shared inlet. Withdrawal only begins after a multi-epoch voyage, and during that wait peers can slash the bond if they prove the same controller is running duplicate identities. The bond is priced in a scarce crystal credit that accrues solely from attested work, so minting thousands of fake agents multiplies locked capital instead of influence. An attacker must fund and freeze a full bond for each shell, which costs more than honest participation.
